# Ply

> Ply is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that keeps your Mac on your iPhone's USB hotspot instead of Wi-Fi, and can combine Wi-Fi + iPhone USB (and Ethernet) so many connections at once use every link. No VPN, no account, no server: everything runs on the Mac.

Ply does three things:
1. USB first: keeps iPhone USB above Wi-Fi in macOS's service order, leaves the iPhone's Wi-Fi hotspot when the cable is up, and can turn Wi-Fi off while on USB.
2. Combine: a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:7591 that sends each new connection over the least-loaded link with internet. Many connections (browsing, multi-stream downloads, speed tests) add up; one single connection stays on one link.
3. Diagnose: explains why USB tethering or Combine is not working, with the action that fixes each problem.

Every action is available four ways with the same names and JSON:
- Menu bar app: Ply.app
- CLI: `ply <command>` (add `--json` for machine output). If `ply` is not on PATH, use `/Applications/Ply.app/Contents/Helpers/ply`.
- MCP (stdio): `ply mcp`; tools are named `ply_<action>`
- HTTP: `POST http://127.0.0.1:7590/v1/actions/<action>` with `Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/Library/Application\ Support/Ply/api-token)`. OpenAPI: `GET /openapi.json`.

## Actions
- `status`: Which connection the Mac is using right now, every link with its live speed, the macOS service order, Combine state, helper state and findings. CLI `ply status [--json|--md]` · MCP `ply_status` · API `POST /v1/actions/status`
- `diagnose`: Explain why iPhone USB or Combine is not working and how to fix it. Each finding names the action that fixes it and includes a ready-to-paste agent prompt. CLI `ply diagnose [--json]` · MCP `ply_diagnose` · API `POST /v1/actions/diagnose`
- `agent_prompt`: A self-contained prompt that describes this Mac's connection state and how to drive Ply, for pasting into any AI agent. CLI `ply agent-prompt` · MCP `ply_agent_prompt` · API `POST /v1/actions/agent_prompt`
- `prefer_usb`: Move every iPhone USB network service above Wi-Fi in macOS's service order and turn off macOS's "Disable unless needed" switch for it, so the cable is used whenever it is connected. Needs the helper. CLI `ply prefer-usb` · MCP `ply_prefer_usb` · API `POST /v1/actions/prefer_usb`
- `combine_start`: Start Combine: a local proxy on 127.0.0.1:7591 spreads new connections across every link with internet (Wi-Fi, iPhone USB, Ethernet) and, with systemProxy, points macOS's auto-proxy at it. A single download stays on one link; many connections add up. CLI `ply combine on [--split connection|site] [--no-system-proxy]` · MCP `ply_combine_start` · API `POST /v1/actions/combine_start`
- `combine_stop`: Stop Combine and restore the proxy settings Ply changed. CLI `ply combine off` · MCP `ply_combine_stop` · API `POST /v1/actions/combine_stop`
- `speed_test`: Measure download speed on each link alone and on all links at once. Uses mobile data on the iPhone link (capped by speedTestMaxMB per link per phase). CLI `ply speedtest [--seconds 5] [--mode both]` · MCP `ply_speed_test` · API `POST /v1/actions/speed_test`
- `set_wifi_power`: Turn the Mac's Wi-Fi radio on or off. CLI `ply wifi on|off` · MCP `ply_set_wifi_power` · API `POST /v1/actions/set_wifi_power`
- `disconnect_wifi`: Disconnect Wi-Fi from its current network (for example the iPhone's own Wi-Fi hotspot) without turning Wi-Fi off. CLI `ply wifi disconnect` · MCP `ply_disconnect_wifi` · API `POST /v1/actions/disconnect_wifi`
- `get_settings`: Read Ply's settings. CLI `ply settings` · MCP `ply_get_settings` · API `POST /v1/actions/get_settings`
- `update_settings`: Change one or more settings. Pass only the keys to change. CLI `ply settings set key=value [key=value ...]` · MCP `ply_update_settings` · API `POST /v1/actions/update_settings`
- `repair_tether`: Turn each iPhone USB network service off and on again to wake a tether that is plugged in but not getting an address. Needs the helper. CLI `ply repair` · MCP `ply_repair_tether` · API `POST /v1/actions/repair_tether`
- `restore_proxies`: Put back every macOS proxy setting Ply changed. Safe to run any time. CLI `ply restore-proxies` · MCP `ply_restore_proxies` · API `POST /v1/actions/restore_proxies`
- `install_helper`: Install Ply's small root helper and the `ply` command (asks for an admin password once). The helper can only reorder network services, point proxies at Ply's local PAC file, restore them, and toggle one service. CLI `ply helper install (or: sudo ply helper install)` · MCP `ply_install_helper` · API `POST /v1/actions/install_helper`
- `uninstall_helper`: Restore proxies, then remove the helper, its LaunchDaemon and the /usr/local/bin/ply link. CLI `ply helper uninstall` · MCP `ply_uninstall_helper` · API `POST /v1/actions/uninstall_helper`
- `set_launch_at_login`: Start the Ply menu bar app when you log in. CLI `ply login-item on|off` · MCP `ply_set_launch_at_login` · API `POST /v1/actions/set_launch_at_login`
- `show_window`: Open Ply's window on the user's screen, with the same controls as the menu bar menu. Use it to show the user what Ply is doing, or when the menu bar icon is hidden because the menu bar is full (common on MacBooks with a notch). Opens Ply.app first if it is not running. CLI `ply open` · MCP `ply_show_window` · API `POST /v1/actions/show_window`
- `about`: Version, license, source code and documentation links. CLI `ply about` · MCP `ply_about` · API `POST /v1/actions/about`
- `quit`: Stop the running Ply engine (app or daemon), restoring any proxy settings first. CLI `ply quit` · MCP `ply_quit` · API `POST /v1/actions/quit`
